faq.q: Why can't an engine turn the wheels from standstill by itself?
faq.a: An engine must keep spinning at several hundred turns a minute to run, but the wheels start at zero. The clutch and a low gear bridge that gap while the car gets moving.
asks: Why does an engine need revs?

faq.q: Why does it take so much force to get a car moving?
faq.a: A car has a lot of mass, often over a tonne, and mass resists changes in motion. Speeding it up from still needs a big force, much more than keeping it rolling steadily.

faq.q: How does first gear multiply turning force?
faq.a: In first gear the engine turns roughly 12 to 15 times for each turn of the wheels, counting the final drive in the axle. Like a lever, the slower output gets a much bigger turning force.
asks: What does a low gear do?

faq.q: Why does a car stall in a high gear?
faq.a: A high gear asks the engine for more turning force than it can make at low speed, so the engine slows below the speed it needs to run and stops. That is called stalling.

faq.q: Do electric cars need first gear?
faq.a: Most electric cars use a single gear, because an electric motor gives strong turning force from standstill and can also spin very fast. So they need no gear changes.
asks: Why do electric cars have no gears?

facts: Most petrol car engines tick over, or idle, at roughly 600 to 1,000 turns per minute.
Most electric cars have a single-speed gearbox because electric motors give strong turning force from standstill.
Every car's axle has a final drive gear that slows the wheels further, multiplying force again.
